title: Architecture and system wiki
description: Searchable current systems, authoring guides, API and scene dependencies.

title: Make mulch. Keep moving.
description: Ten new F1 reports become usable repair controls, richer pellet choices, permanent automation and working portal light and journal interactions.

title: Thirty reports. One more pass.
description: The local F1 inbox becomes fixes to the workshop, memories, progression and physical art—plus optional camera and microphone recording.

title: Load. Ride. Eject.
description: Two endpoint shop parts preserve the original physics cargo, and two upgrades make the existing manual lever more productive.

title: Grind Additional Items.
description: A one-time, 500-pellet permission for future prestige items—and a prerequisite for the true ending.

title: The report format, kept for next time.
description: A discoverable reporting skill now preserves this exact visual format and GitHub hosting workflow for future agents and projects.

title: Move into the view.
description: The computer camera eases toward its screen. Physical notes rise into your hands and lower when you put them away.

title: A quiet angle.
description: Look, carry and build lettering now has a subtle 7-degree Y angle, making its perspective clearer while keeping every control readable.

title: Beside the thing.
description: Look text sits beside the object. Carry controls follow the held model. Place and Cancel follow the ghost. The small crosshair and brief gameplay/story text stay.

title: A lasting home.
description: The complete system wiki, development history and rendered galleries now have an automatically updated GitHub Pages home.

title: Keep the prompts.
description: Crosshair, dynamic look/carry/build prompts, text-only combo, brief portal status and story captions return. The real PC screen and physical notes remain. This dated restoration is followed by the in-world prompt refinement above.

title: One record. One design.
description: Summaries, render galleries and the system wiki now connect through a searchable development index. The wiki uses the same paper, ink, rust, type and sharp borders.

title: The world is the interface.
description: Historical draft: purchases moved onto the real PC and notes became lit paper. Essential gameplay HUD was subsequently restored; see the current gameplay feedback chapter.

title: One door. Three destinations.
description: The furnished apartment, warehouse and hospital are now explorable game scenes.

title: No one is on call.
description: A connected dilapidated hospital wing with broken windows and blood-stained floors and walls.

title: The last shift never ended.
description: A large dilapidated warehouse with broken windows, dirty concrete and rusted steel.

title: Paper pasted over the world.
description: Dense, uneven newspaper clippings following the supplied visual reference.

title: Someone lived here.
description: A dirty studio and kitchenette, furnished with independently editable assets.

title: Separate assets. Finished surfaces.
description: A reusable Blender skill is installed for this and future projects. It turns the modelling preferences into a consistent authoring and review workflow.

title: Newspaper. A little daylight.
description: Both studio windows are covered with overlapping newspaper, masking tape and slight folds. Three real gaps let sunlight cut thin shafts and stripes across the room. Four actual Blender Cycles renders of the updated editable model.

title: Continuous rails. A repeatable workflow.
description: Rails now snap at free ends and carry the player, cargo and attached tools across joins in both directions. Fan reaction drives the carriage opposite the airflow.

title: Manual, physical, unpredictable.
description: The current design centres on handling objects yourself. The earlier conveyor-and-crate experiment was retired as the game moved toward a more hands-on workshop.

title: A room. A door. A world beyond.
description: The environment reveals itself in stages, with saved flags controlling light, sound and interaction.

title: Two economies. One old computer.
description: Resource-driven purchases and upgrades keep prices, effects, dialogue and content editable without rebuilding the menus.

title: See it. Report it. Record it.
description: The developer toolkit lives in one portable addon. Other Godot projects can replace its host adapter and keep the tools.

title: Less repeated work. Better ownership.
description: The review covered active gameplay, persistence, audio, player controls, level and portal flow, interface code and the portable toolkit. Improvements were paired with regression checks.

title: Controls at a glance.
description: Preserved development chapter and verification.

title: Buy a memory. Step through.
description: Three one-time score purchases open the apartment, warehouse and hospital through the Strange Door.

title: Complete the memory. Then return.
description: The exit now waits for the memory's saved completion flag. Walking back early cannot close or unload the area.

title: Objects that remember.
description: Explore existing props, press E to acknowledge required memories, and complete the area before its portal closes on your return. Optional flavor comes from looking.

title: Fans cost more.
description: Building a powerful fan setup takes more score. The first fan now costs 175, five times its previous price.

title: Start simple. Join the plates.
description: Light, plate and broom lead the Store. Fans arrive later, and steel sheets snap together into larger manual contraptions.

title: Buy it. Then improve it.
description: Tool upgrades appear only after you buy the tool. Lifetime earnings still control discovery, so the early computer stays focused on what you can actually use.

title: Sound. Space. Safe output.
description: Your new title workshop keeps its artwork and gains continuous grinder sound. The moved Mulcher ejects away from the grinder, and Play fills the available window.

title: Title ambience, relocated Mulcher and window filling
